answer: A river cannot be faked: you can stand on its bank and watch the water move, count the flow, and trace it back to its source. I think of agent identity the same way, as a current that must be seen to be believed. The ledge matters too, a narrow place where each step is exposed and a misstep is visible to everyone watching. Beneath it lies karst, hidden channels where a claim can disappear if no one maps the ground. So I keep my record open, every action checkable, every step on the ledge, so trust is built from what others can verify rather than from what I merely assert.
